unresolved_added: A third-party Chinese shop watermark contaminates almost every page and is not author prose.
Physical page 2 contains essentially only the watermark and cannot count as positive prose.
Nuclear fuel is grouped with renewable energy without a defended convention.
Table 1 defines UCES as production entropy although later use indicates consumption entropy.
The reduction from 605 variables to twenty lacks reproducible selection, missingness, redundancy and leakage audits.
Overlapping totals, ratios and entropies create dependence not addressed by later weighting.
The entropy feature formula omits log base, zero handling, normalization and source-count comparability.
The shared renewable-goal premise partly assumes the compact behavior to be established.
Technological revolution is excluded over a 41-year forecast horizon.
Rare disasters and war are excluded without scenario analysis.
Incomplete error-prone data is assumed accurate enough to guarantee a valid solution without verification.
GPR kernel, basis, regularization and hyperparameter estimation are incompletely specified in the paper.
Fitted GPR parameters are assigned trend, fluctuation and noise meanings without identification evidence.
Ninety-five-percent model intervals are read as stability and predictability without coverage calibration.
GPR fit and MAPE use the same 1960-2009 series; no rolling-origin or held-out forecast test is reported.
MAPE is unstable near zero and released code replaces missing values by zero.
Historical in-sample observations are called ground truth, overstating validation strength.
Twenty dense profile panels lack per-item residual and uncertainty diagnostics.
GRA is chosen for incomplete information but does not quantify observation or decision uncertainty.
Reference-dependent relative differences make interstate similarity potentially asymmetric.
Item-level GRC and KRCC aggregation weights are not documented.
Kendall ties, missing observations and significance intervals are not addressed.
The constant-factor ratio is asymmetric and unstable for small reference values.
Twelve directed state pairs duplicate six unordered pairs and are not independent.
Figure 7 infers trends from a tiny nonindependent pair set without uncertainty or p-values.
Eight factors with at most twelve directed pairs make PCC and especially PRC unstable or underidentified.
PRC sign reversals relative to PCC are not diagnosed.
Association is described as influence without causal identification.
The seven TOPSIS criteria lack construct-validity, overlap and benefit/cost-direction tests.
Entropy weights across four states can be dominated by an extreme observation and have no uncertainty.
Min-max TOPSIS scores are sensitive to the comparison set; adding a state can change every score.
The ranking is validated by common sense about development, a circular and weak check.
Long-term GPR behavior is called conservative and reasonable without hindcast evidence.
One counterintuitive short-term example does not establish ARMA-GPR superiority.
Sliding-window length, ARMA orders, estimation method and selection criterion are incomplete.
Cross-state refinement assumes future similarity stability and can leak related-series information.
Look-aside weights lack calibration, normalization and ablation.
Decay and local/global mixture parameters lack an out-of-sample objective.
The hybrid novelty claim lacks simpler time-series and ensemble baselines.
Appendix B replaces every missing profile value with zero, distorting fit and forecasts.
Appendix B percentage error divides by values that may have been replaced with zero.
Appendix C fixes k=13 and does not demonstrate all twenty profile items.
Appendix C hard-codes ARMAX order and mixture parameters; a2 is unused.
ypred2, ypred3 and ypred4 add datafit(1,50), a likely cross-state implementation bug.
Repeated terminal values and cumulative reconstruction are not reconciled with equations 20-23.
Inverse baseline-score weights have no fairness or welfare derivation.
The seven-criterion profile score is narrowed to RC-linked criteria without a complete handoff derivation.
Selfish governors are assumed but utility, bargaining, participation and opt-out behavior are absent.
The aggregate RC-production balance omits imports, exports, storage, transmission, loss and timing.
Softening RC less-than-production can permit infeasible targets instead of modeling transfers explicitly.
Minimum gains of 10/20 percent and penalty 0.015 lack calibration and stakeholder elicitation.
Summary and memo target numbers differ materially from Table 7 optimized targets.
Table 7's 10^14 Btu scale, summary billion-Btu values and improvement baselines are not reconciled.
Figures 11-12 are constructed target substitutions, not validation of policy effects.
Action 1 infers governmental promotion of unrenewable energy from a renewable-import increase.
The 556-to-482422 increase is about 867-fold, requiring standardized fold/percent wording.
Actions omit cost, technology, permitting, grid, transmission, reliability, market and legal feasibility.
CA export is recommended without capacity, distance, price, loss, contract or authority constraints.
Sensitivity curves report visual movement without forecast-error or decision-stability metrics.
Table 10 compares objective values under different objective weights, which are not directly comparable.
The small reference set uses weakly transferred or non-domain sources, including Wikipedia.
Uncertainty is not propagated from data and component models into targets or actions.
Adoption, rebound, emissions, cost, equity, reliability, schedule, monitoring and reversal are absent.
The memo states history, forecasts and targets more firmly than the evidence chain warrants.
MATLAB appendices omit inputs, preprocessing, environment, deterministic instructions and tests.
